channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Transport Minister Discusses Road Paving Plans and Progress
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has approximately 35,000 kilometers of roads, with over 9,000 km currently paved. The Ministry of Transport aims to pave all remaining gravel roads, including those leading to pastures, by building 1.5-2 thousand kilometers annually. The 2024 budget allocates 62.2 billion soms for road construction and repair.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways Reports Significant Profit Growth Despite 3.9 Trillion Debt
item.description: Kazakhstan Railways (KTZ) reported a net profit of 343.6 billion tenge in 2025, a 2.1-fold increase, despite a total debt of 3.9 trillion tenge. Growth was driven by increased freight and transit tariffs, while passenger transport incurred a loss subsidized by the state.

item.title: New Electronic Queue Customs Terminal Opens at Ken-Sai Border Crossing with Uzbekistan
item.description: A new customs terminal and electronic queue zone for vehicles has opened at the Ken-Sai international border crossing between Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan. The facility aims to streamline traffic flow and reduce waiting times, incorporating digital management systems and service areas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Consumer Prices Rose 8.8% Year-to-Date Through October
item.description: Consumer prices and tariffs in Kyrgyzstan increased by 8.8% from January to October 2026 compared to December 2025, according to the National Statistical Committee. Food prices rose 7.7%, alcohol and tobacco 8%, non-food goods 7.6%, and services 12.12%. Prices for fresh vegetables, potatoes, and rice decreased.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Detains District Officials in Illegal Gold Mining Corruption Scheme
item.description: The head of Chatkal district and the local police chief in Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad region have been detained on suspicion of involvement in an illegal gold mining corruption scheme. The Interior Ministry is investigating a criminal case for corruption, alleging a group illegally extracted gold without licenses and paid officials for protection.

item.title: Pakistan Security Forces Neutralize 24 Suspects in Counter-Terrorism Operations
item.description: Pakistan's security forces eliminated 24 individuals suspected of terrorism in operations across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan provinces. Four soldiers were killed during clashes. The military claimed that groups responsible for attacks received support from Indian special services, though this remains unverified.

item.title: Russia Sees 13-Fold Increase in Rejections for Residence Permits, Third Drop in Citizenship
item.description: Russia has seen a 13-fold increase in rejections for residence permits and a one-third decrease in citizenship grants over the past year, according to Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev. The ministry also proposed expanding a system for tracking migrants via mobile app nationwide, currently in a Moscow experiment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's GDP Exceeds 1.8 Trillion Som Since Early 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) reached 1.866 trillion som in January-October 2026, a 10.5% increase from the previous year, according to the National Statistical Committee. Services accounted for over 48.9% of the total GDP.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Ban on Exporting Young Cattle for Six Months
item.description: Kazakhstan has extended the ban on exporting young cattle, including to EAEU countries, for another six months from November 9, 2026. The Ministry of Agriculture signed the relevant order. The country continues to export other types of livestock and poultry.

item.title: Retail Trade Future in Central Asia Discussed by Umai Group Chairman Rud Pedersen
item.description: Rud Pedersen, Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Umai Group, shared insights on the future of retail in Central Asia in an interview with European Supermarket Magazine. He discussed the growth of Umai Group and the region's potential, emphasizing the sector's contribution to the economy.

item.title: Atyrau Develops Railcar Manufacturing, Expanding Beyond Oil Industry
item.description: Atyrau, Kazakhstan, is developing heavy machinery manufacturing, focusing on railcar production. The TEXOL company's Atyrau Railcar Plant produces five freight cars every 12 hours. The industrial cluster includes a wheelset workshop, testing center, and repair facilities, with plans for a foundry.

item.title: Kazakh President Sends Congratulatory Message to Palestinian President on Independence Day
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has congratulated Mahmoud Abbas and the Palestinian people on their Independence Day. Tokayev expressed confidence that Abbas's leadership will foster national unity, strengthen sovereignty, and promote socio-economic development, leading to enhanced bilateral relations. He wished Abbas success and the Palestinian people prosperity.

item.title: Osh Plans Construction of Two Modern Cable Cars to Boost Tourism
item.description: Osh city plans to build two modern cable cars to increase tourist flow and enhance its tourism potential. Preliminary designs suggest one cable car route from the Yugo-Vostok microdistrict along the Ak-Buura river to the Navoi park, and another from the Kerme-Too mountain. Construction is expected to begin in spring.

item.title: 23 Construction Sites Inspected in Issyk-Kul Region
item.description: In the Issyk-Kul region, 23 construction sites were inspected by the Ministry of Construction. The inspections focused on compliance with design documents, construction norms, safety regulations, and new requirements. Several specific sites, including resort centers and apartment buildings, were examined for adherence to standards.

item.title: Israel Warns US of Potential Iranian Plot Against Trump
item.description: Israel has shared intelligence with the US indicating a potential Iranian plot to assassinate President Donald Trump and other American officials, according to Israel Hayom. The report suggests Iran may use drones for attacks. Following the warning, security for several high-ranking US officials has been increased.

item.title: NATO to Reduce Summits and Ministerial Meetings Amid Disagreements
item.description: NATO is reducing the number of its summits and ministerial meetings due to disagreements, according to AP. The alliance is also decreasing the frequency of foreign ministers' gatherings. A summit planned for Albania in 2027 has been canceled. NATO attributes this decision to restructuring efforts.

item.title: Tajikistan Excluded from World Tourism Development Index 2026
item.description: Tajikistan did not make the 2026 Travel & Tourism Development Index (TTDI) by the World Economic Forum and Zurich Insurance Group. The report included 110 countries, with Kazakhstan at 56th, Uzbekistan 76th, and Kyrgyzstan 93rd. Tajikistan was 99th in the 2024 index. Reasons for exclusion were not specified, but criteria include participation in surveys and data completeness.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Tashkent Region Explores Hotel and Textile Projects with Japanese Firm
item.description: Japanese company Belluna Co., Ltd. is considering investments in Tashkent Region, Uzbekistan, focusing on four-star hotels and textile production. Discussions included land allocation, infrastructure, and export opportunities for local goods like cotton apparel and dried fruits to Japan.

item.title: Diplomatic Engagements in Abu Dhabi, Moscow, and Dublin Signal New Peace Process for Ukraine War
item.description: Renewed diplomatic activity involving the US, Russia, and Ukraine, with talks in Abu Dhabi, Moscow, and Dublin, suggests a new process aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war. The US views the conflict as a strategic issue for European security.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Attends ECO Meeting in Pakistan
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to Pakistan to attend the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO). He is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with officials from participating countries on the sidelines of the event.

item.title: Russia Claims Air Defense Systems Shot Down 230 Ukrainian Drones in One Day
item.description: Russia's Defence Ministry reported that its air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 230 Ukrainian drones within a 12-hour period on Sunday. The drones were reportedly downed over Crimea, Belgorod, Bryansk, Kursk regions, and the Black Sea.

item.title: Iran Offers Agricultural Training and Investment to Afghanistan
item.description: Iran's Minister of Agriculture Jihad, Gholamreza Nouri Ghezeljeh, stated Iran's readiness to cooperate with the Taliban on agricultural training and investment. Several Iranian companies are prepared to invest and expand operations in Afghanistan. Annual trade between Iran and the Taliban stands at $2.7 billion, with agricultural products comprising a quarter of this total.

item.title: Russia Demands NATO Withdrawal from Central Asia in Ukraine Peace Talks
item.description: During peace negotiations concerning Ukraine, Russia presented demands that extend beyond Ukraine and Europe, impacting Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan. These demands, outlined in an unofficial document, include NATO's withdrawal from Central Asia and the Caucasus, and a return to pre-1997 NATO military presence levels.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Oversees Agricultural Sector Progress
item.description: President Serdar Berdimuhamedov held a video conference to discuss agricultural matters. Key focuses included ensuring efficient cotton harvesting, timely wheat sowing, and proper field care. Payments to producers and service providers were also addressed. Specific attention was given to cotton and sugar beet harvests in various regions.

item.title: Iran: Russia and China Deem US Regional Actions Illegal
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated that Russia and China consider US unilateral policies responsible for regional developments. Moscow and Beijing oppose Washington's confrontational approach, viewing US actions as illegal and ill-considered. Iran maintains close contact with Russia and China as strategic partners, with ongoing consultations on regional issues.

item.title: Taliban to Attend Upcoming Economic Cooperation Organization Meeting in Iran
item.description: The Taliban announced they will participate in the upcoming Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) meeting in Tehran. This marks a shift from the previous ECO summit in Islamabad, where the Taliban were not invited. The meeting is scheduled for December.

item.title: Kazakh Judoka Yerassyl Kazhybayev to Compete for Bronze in Zagreb
item.description: Kazakhstan's judoka Yerassyl Kazhybayev will compete for a bronze medal at the Grand Prix tournament in Zagreb, Croatia. He will face Saba Inaneishvili of Georgia in the over 100kg category. Aida Toishybekova also competed but was eliminated.

item.title: Iran Rejects Germany's Call to Halt Uranium Enrichment, Cites NPT Rights
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei rejected Germany's demand to stop uranium enrichment, asserting Iran's right under the NPT. He criticized the IAEA's speculation about a new facility and warned that Tehran will respond to any attacks.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Legal Literacy Program in All Schools
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a legal literacy program in all schools, from the first to the eleventh grade. The program aims to promote legal awareness through practical exercises, including guidance on whom to contact and how to seek help when rights are violated. Details are available on daryo.uz.

item.title: ECO Ministerial Meeting Begins in Islamabad Without Afghan Representation
item.description: The 24th ECO Ministerial Meeting commenced in Islamabad, Pakistan, without representatives from Afghanistan. The Taliban's deputy foreign minister implicitly confirmed their non-invitation, stating regional integration without Afghanistan is a 'false dream'. Pakistan's Foreign Ministry confirmed participation from member states' foreign ministers and heads of delegations.

item.title: Afghanistan and Uzbekistan Agree on 100,000 Tons of Potato Exports
item.description: Afghanistan and Uzbekistan have reached an agreement for the export of 100,000 tons of potatoes from the Bamyan province. This deal aims to support Afghan farmers and boost agricultural trade between the two neighboring countries.

item.title: Iran Claims Drone Attack on US Military Base in Bahrain, Responding to US Strike
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for a drone attack on a radar station at a US military base in Bahrain, stating it was retaliation for a US strike on an Iranian communication facility in Sirik. Bahraini authorities reported intercepting multiple objects in their airspace and raised the military's readiness level.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Become a Leading Global Textile Industry Center
item.description: Uzbekistan, historically a major cotton producer, is transitioning from raw material export to a high-value-added textile industry. Following independence, steps were taken to develop the sector, but raw cotton exports dominated. Since 2020, a ban on raw cotton fiber exports has spurred domestic processing into yarn, fabrics, and finished garments, positioning Uzbekistan as a significant industrial center.

item.title: Taliban Authorities to Meet in Kabul to Discuss Leader's Decrees
item.description: Taliban authorities and supporters are expected to gather at Kabul’s Loya Jirga Hall for a meeting. The meeting aims to promote the implementation of decrees issued by their leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada. Sources within the Taliban confirmed the gathering is scheduled for Monday, Nov. 16.

item.title: Georgia and Turkey Share Common Values and Political Approaches, Says Kavelashvili
item.description: Georgian President Mikhail Kavelashvili stated that close cooperation exists between Tbilisi and Ankara, covering a wide range of areas. Speaking at COP31 in Antalya, he expressed satisfaction with his meeting with Turkish President Erdoğan, describing him as a great friend. Kavelashvili emphasized that both nations share common values and similar political approaches, prioritizing peace, stability, and national identity.

item.title: Uzbekistan President to Visit Oman on State Visit
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, will visit Oman on November 16–17 at the invitation of Sultan Haitham bin Tarik Al Said. Bilateral high-level negotiations, meetings with major company leaders, and other events will take place in Muscat. The summit agenda includes elevating Uzbek-Omani relations and expanding cooperation in trade, investment, and agriculture.

item.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Claim Drone Attack on US Radar Facility in Bahrain
item.description: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed it targeted a US radar defense facility at Al-Riffa Air Base in Bahrain using six drones. Anadolu Agency reported that no details were provided about damage or casualties. Bahrain's Interior Ministry had issued warnings prior to the incident. The IRGC also stated the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

item.title: Taliban Plan Gathering to Promote Leader's Decrees, Sources Say
item.description: Taliban authorities and supporters are expected to gather in Kabul to promote the implementation of decrees issued by their leader, Hibatullah Akhundzada. The meeting, scheduled for November 16, will focus on enforcing the leader's directives and discussing a book attributed to him. Security measures have been tightened around the venue.

item.title: UNESCO and Uzbekistan Forge Path Towards Global Dialogue
item.description: Uzbekistan joined UNESCO in 1993, leveraging its rich history to share its cultural heritage globally. Key collaborations include the inscription of historical sites like Ichan-Kala in Khiva, Bukhara, and Shakhrisabz, and Samarkand on the World Heritage List. Intangible cultural heritage elements such as "Shashmaqom" and "Navruz" are also recognized. Samarkand will host the 43rd UNESCO General Conference in 2025.

item.title: India Forms Special Units for Potential Border Clashes with China
item.description: India is establishing special units to prepare for potential border clashes with China. Soldiers are being trained for movement and drone surveillance in mountainous regions. Disagreements persist between the two nations over their shared border.
